name: Skyways Air Services Limited
key_reason: The engine moved to CONSIDER on the final book and I will not argue with the demand, but my own call stays NEUTRAL. A 2.1% net margin business at roughly 31.6x earnings has no margin of safety if freight rates move against it, and heavy last-day bidding does not change that arithmetic.

name: Symbiotec Pharmalab Limited
key_reason: I am keeping AVOID even though the engine has moved to NEUTRAL on the strength of the final book. The disagreement is deliberate and I want it visible: none of the reasons to avoid this issue changed during the afternoon. 91.5% of the money still goes to exiting shareholders, the promoter still leaves entirely, 13.22% of pre-offer capital is still pledged, and two lead managers still have interests on the other side of the table. Heavy institutional bidding on the last afternoon is a bet on the listing, not a verdict on the company you would be left holding.

name: Hy Tech Engineers Limited
key_reason: The engine moved to APPLY once the final book was in, and I agree. The valuation is genuinely below peers, returns are strong and institutions committed at the close. The concentration risk on customers, suppliers and the US affiliate is the reason to size any application modestly rather than the reason to skip it.

name: Annu Projects Limited
key_reason: NEUTRAL stands. This is the one issue where you would get essentially the full allotment you ask for - which cuts both ways. Full allotment of something the market is avoiding is not a bargain by itself.

name: Lumino Industries Limited
key_reason: This one exposed a real bug rather than a judgement call. The engine originally scored it NEUTRAL because the book stood at 0.22x - but bidding had opened that morning, and the rule could not tell 'nobody wants it' from 'it opened an hour ago'. Subscription scoring is now window-aware, and the engine independently reaches CONSIDER. The customer concentration on government and PSU clients remains the real risk, so size any application modestly and re-check the book on the final day.

name: Kwick Forensic Solutions Limited
key_reason: CONSIDER matches the computed verdict, but the SME caveat does most of the work here. The growth is real; the risk is that Rs 1.44 lakh buys an illiquid position in a company where three-quarters of revenue sits with ten customers. Only sensible if that sum is genuinely discretionary for you.

name: Priority Jewels Limited
key_reason: CONSIDER, matching the computed verdict. The growth is real and the all-fresh structure is genuinely shareholder-friendly. The single-city manufacturing concentration is the risk to weigh, and it is not something a subscription figure captures.

name: Esds Software Solution Limited
key_reason: I disagree with the computed NEUTRAL and would call this CONSIDER. The engine penalises the 41.6x multiple using fixed P/E bands that take no account of growth - and profit here more than doubled year on year. That is a known limitation of the valuation axis, not a judgement about this company. The risk is real though: at this multiple you are paying in advance for execution.

name: Paluck Technologies Limited
key_reason: I am stepping this down from the computed APPLY to CONSIDER. The margin trajectory is real and the demand is strong, but the compliance history is a governance signal the engine is blind to, and Rs 1.44 lakh into an illiquid SME on that basis is not a decision to take on a score alone. Read the RHP risk factors before applying.

name: Complete Sports And Management India Limited
key_reason: NEUTRAL stands. The margin improvement is real but revenue is barely moving, and the book has attracted very little interest so far. There is no case here for committing Rs 1.35 lakh to an illiquid SME on present evidence.
